ideas.title: Climb anything: the first real hang
ideas.critique: This is a real step on from the debug still: Lumi's body carries load through friction contacts and can actually fall, which the island has never done. The risk is that a film of one hang turns into a scripted-looking grab. If the slip never shows on camera, it reads as an animation of the dots from last time.

ideas.title: A burning glass
ideas.critique: Fire that spreads is an example the goals name outright ('burn'), so it is expected however well it is done. The sun caustic is the one surprising part, and it only counts if the hot spot really comes out of the traced lens and is not a cursor dot. Fire on a fuel grid with wind and slope that you have to contain is strong play.

ideas.title: Footprints that tell on you
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Ground that keeps plastic dents in it is a new kind of layer, and prints that tell you weight and gait are a clever use of physics. The detective game is a single fixed mystery, though, so it plays once, and in a still the dents can easily look like decals.

ideas.title: Sailing against the wind
ideas.critique: Apparent-wind lift with luffing, keel drift and heel is a skill players get better at, which is rare on this island. It holds up only if the raft floats on the real sea surface; a raft gliding on a flat plane with a scripted heel would make it a toy. A chase-camera zigzag is the expected shot.

ideas.title: Sandcastle against the tide
ideas.critique: Granular sand with moisture cohesion would be the island's first continuum solid, and a collapse you lose differently every time is a good loop. It hinges on an MPM that runs live at beach scale. A slump driven by a heightfield would be the island-wrecking cliché the island has done before with dunes and floods.

ideas.title: Stones that ring
same_form: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: Pitch from each mesh's real eigenmodes is engineering the island has never had, and you can verify it by ear. It is still the third acoustic piece in a short span, and a film with sound is the one form the reviewers cannot see. The xylophone goal gives a reason to come back but stays a gentle toy.

ideas.title: A snowball that grows
same_form: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is one rolling object going downhill, filmed from above, the same shape as the sun-ball films, with a growing radius as the twist. The snow layer carved down to grass is the new part. The snowman knock-over sits close to a scripted payoff.

ideas.title: Tightrope between two trees
ideas.critique: A ragdoll balancing on a sagging rope is a real control problem, and real falls are good to watch. The active ragdoll it depends on does not exist yet, though. If balance gets faked with a tilt variable, it turns into a canned wobble animation on a line.

ideas.title: Fell a tree into a bridge
ideas.critique: Breaking is an example the goals name, so the idea is capped. The hinge wood steering the fall is the one real mechanism in it. A tree that becomes a bridge is a satisfying cause-and-effect, but it is used once per tree, and the fall will look like a joint that snaps from a scripted angle unless the cut geometry really sets it.

ideas.title: Herding bees with smoke
ideas.critique: Volumetric smoke drifting in the island's wind is new and could look beautiful traced. But bees made of dots are the same swarm-of-specks picture the fireflies failed on, and herding with an avoidance rule tends to play as pushing a blob.
